title: Canonical shifted common-core form comparison and two-orientation inclusion contract
question: Does the EXP-001129 form envelope yield a positive canonical shift, a common-core local form comparison, and bounded two-orientation square-root inclusion constants?

model.core: D=C_c^infinity(R^2) for the two-site position representation, with q_i multiplication and p_i=-i*d/dq_i
model.weights: K_on=H_on+11/6 I and K_edge=H_on+B+11/6 I, so both are >= I on the closed form domains
model.orientation_contract: The Friedrichs form closures imply ||K_edge^(1/2) K_on^(-1/2)|| <= sqrt(224/45) and ||K_on^(1/2) K_edge^(-1/2)|| <= 1, subject to the declared closure/product-domain hypotheses.

adversarial_review.check: The negative r term is completed against the quartic exactly, giving -5/12 per site and -5/6 per edge.
The shift 11/6 is chosen so both K_on and K_edge dominate I; no spectral minimum is silently assumed.
The form comparison is on C_c^infinity and the square-root inclusion is explicitly a Friedrichs/product-domain contract, not an unconditional operator theorem.
The local constants are independent of source and volume, while cutoff and beta transfer remain open.
Both K_edge over K_on and K_on over K_edge directions are retained; the latter uses bond positivity.
Common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks exact rational lower-bound and comparison arithmetic only; it does not formalize unbounded operators or Friedrichs domains.

qft_interface.closed: A canonical source- and volume-independent local form comparison with explicit two-orientation square-root inclusion constants, conditional on standard closed-form/product-domain hypotheses.
qft_interface.open: Friedrichs realization and product-domain proof for the exact Q3 common core, cutoff/beta modular transfer, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, exhaustion, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS identification, gap and continuum.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: No heat_root_incidence or canonical A1/R-192 production owner is supplied.

no_overclaim: This is a form-level common-core comparison and conditional square-root inclusion contract. It is not yet an unconditional operator-domain theorem, thermodynamic QFT dynamics, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, a gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A result.
